edition.name: Migne, Patrologia Latina (PL 2, Paris 1844), De virginibus velandis, via Latin Wikisource transcription
edition.witness_note: Single locked witness in repo; second witness not yet locked.

source_text: Si propter homines habitu abutuntur, impleant illum etiam in hoc, ut et apud ethnicos caput velent. Certe in ecclesia virginitatem suam abscondant, quam extra ecclesiam celant. Timent extraneos, revereantur et fratres: aut constanter audeant, et in vicis virgines videri sicut audent in ecclesiis. Laudabo vigorem, si aliquid et apud ethnicos virginitatis nundinarent. Eadem natura foris quae et intus, eadem institutio apud homines et apud Dominum eadem libertate constat. Quo ergo foris quidem bonum suum abstrudunt, in ecclesia vero provulgant? Exposco rationem; utrumne ut fratribus suis placeant, an ut ipsi Deo? Si ut ipsi Deo: tam idoneus est ad conspicienda quae in occulto fiunt, quam justus ad remuneranda quae soli sibi fiunt. Denique praecipit, nihil debuccinemus eorum quae apud illum mercedem merebuntur, nec ea ab hominibus compensemus. Quod si unius victoriati, vel quamcunque eleemosynae operationem, sinistra conscia facere prohibemur, quantum tenebrarum circumfundere debemus, cum tantam oblationem Deo offerimus, ipsius corporis et ipsius spiritus nostri, cum illam ipsam naturam consecramus. Ergo quod non potest videri propter Deum fieri, quia sic fieri Deus non vult, sequitur ut hominum gratia fiat: utique primo illicitum, ut gloriae libidinosum. Gloria enim illicitum est eis, quorum probatio in omni humiliatione constat. Et si a Deo confertur continentiae virtus; Quid gloriaris quasi non acceperis? Si vero non accepisti, quid habes quod datum tibi non est? Hoc ipso autem constat a Deo datam tibi non esse, quod illam non soli Deo praestas. Videamus ergo quod humanum est, an firmum sit et verum.
pass_a_gloss: If they misuse the habit because of men, let them also fulfill it in this, so that they may also veil their head among the Gentiles. Certainly in the church they should hide their virginity, which they conceal outside the church. They fear strangers, let them also reverence brothers; or let them consistently dare, and be seen as virgins in the streets just as they dare in the churches. I will praise their vigor, if they also peddle something of their virginity among the Gentiles. The same nature is outside which is also inside, the same institution is established among men and among the Lord with the same freedom. So why do they hide their good outside, but proclaim it in the church? I demand a reason; is it so that they may please their brothers, or so that they may please God Himself? If so that they may please God Himself: He is just as able to see what is done in secret, as He is just to reward what is done for Him alone. Finally, He commands that we should not broadcast those things which will earn a reward with Him, nor should we compensate them with human praise. But if we are forbidden to do even a single act of charity with a consciousness of sin, how much more should we shroud in darkness, when we offer to God such a great oblation, of our own body and our own spirit, when we consecrate that very nature. Therefore, what cannot be seen to be done for God, because God does not will it to be done thus, it follows that it is done for the sake of men: certainly first it is unlawful, as it is lustful for glory. For glory is unlawful to those whose proof consists in all humility. And if the virtue of continence is conferred by God; why do you boast as if you had not received it? If you have not received it, why do you have what has not been given to you? But this very thing is established to be given to you by God, in that you do not present it to God alone. Let us see, therefore, what is human, whether it is firm and true.

choices.why: nundinare means to peddle or sell
provulgo means to proclaim or make public

pass_b_english: If you misuse the habit to impress people, then live up to it in this way too: veil your head among the Gentiles. In church you hide your virginity, which you conceal outside of church. You fear strangers; reverence your brothers as well. Or be consistent: dare to be seen as virgins in the streets just as you dare in the churches. I'll praise your mettle if you also peddle your virginity among the Gentiles. The same nature exists outside as inside; the same institution stands among men and before the Lord with the same freedom. So why do you hide your good outside, but broadcast it in church? I demand an answer: is it to please your brothers, or to please God Himself? If it's to please God: He is just as able to see what is done in secret as He is just to reward what is done for Him alone. Finally, He commands us not to broadcast the deeds that will earn a reward from Him, nor to settle for human praise instead. If we're forbidden to perform even a single act of charity with a guilty conscience, how much more must we shroud ourselves in darkness when we offer God so great an oblation—our own body and our own spirit—when we consecrate that very nature? Therefore, what cannot be seen as done for God, because God does not will it to be done that way, follows as done for the sake of men: certainly first it is unlawful, as it is lustful for glory. For glory is unlawful to those whose proof consists in all humility. And if the virtue of continence is conferred by God, why do you boast as if you had not received it? If you haven't received it, what do you have that was not given to you? But this very fact proves it was not given to you by God, because you do not present it to God alone. Let us see, then, what is human, whether it is firm and true.
